out_of_schema_notes: ProcessParameter.target_value and NOR are the set-point and NOR in force, which this revision changed for inactivation pH (set-point and NOR), hold time (set-point and NOR) and temperature (NOR). The studies were planned and run against the set-points and NORs as characterized; each multivariate parameter also anchors on its row of the table of set-points and ranges as characterized and in force, and the three decisions that produced the values in force are report statements. ProcessParameter.PAR is the NOR-propagated XMuLV PAR of a multivariate parameter, the range carried into the control strategy, and the range studied for A-Mab concentration. rationale_for_criticality carries the classification argument of Section 9, each parameter anchored on its own sentences of it.

The QualityAttribute records are the four attributes judged at the output of the step. acceptance_criteria holds the drug substance criterion of the CQA register and the Version 2.0 intermediate acceptance criterion of the step; acceptance_criteria (the annex layer) holds the rows of the criteria-change table, Version 1.0 superseded and Version 2.0 in force.

proven_acceptable_ranges: the three rows of the PAR table (XMuLV clearance, from the selected model), with par_at_setpoint and par_nor_propagated as the columns 'PAR (set-point)' and 'PAR (NOR)' print them, and the three aggregate ranges the text states ('its PAR is the range studied in all three'), both analyses equal to the range studied in doe_report.par_table. Acidic variants and fragments set no PAR (an explicit non-claim). The report's description of the two analyses is recorded in its own words, in report statements anchored on the sentences and figure captions that give it.

The schema has no record type for a discrepancy from the plan. PD-006-01 to PD-006-08 are report statements anchored on their rows of the discrepancy register, and the studies they add carry that row as a source reference.

The report records no deviation: a characterization study is not GMP manufacture, so the two events of execution are study events, under the numbers Version 1.0 gave them (DEV-006-01, DEV-006-02). They are Deviation records, the schema's only record type for an event of execution. no_impact_on_conclusions is true for DEV-006-01, whose effect the report bounds below the margins of the claim and of the aggregate criterion, and false for DEV-006-02, of which the report says only that it can make a computed log reduction smaller and is one possible contributor to the larger pH effect of the screening design.

Studies: every row of the execution-window table with a schema study type has a StudyDesign record. S-VI-OFAT (the new pH set-point against the former one, over hold times) is one_factor_at_a_time; the hold study S-VI-HLD has no hold study type and is recorded as univariate (hold time at two temperatures, factors that are not process parameters). S-CEX-VER and S-VI-WC (verification runs at one setting) and the nrCE-SDS re-test S-VI-RET have no schema study type and no study record; their windows, rules and results are report statements anchored on their rows. Only the two designs carry n_runs, which the corpus test reserves for the seeded DoE designs.

StatisticalModelFit: the planned full quadratic of each output (the re-evaluation table), the selected models of aggregate and of the XMuLV log reduction (all four adequacy criteria met), the selected models of fragments (not adequate, limit on overfitting) and of acidic variants (exact fit, not adequate), and the three screening models. A p-value printed as '< 0.001' has no float value; its term carries significant=true.

parameter_impacts_attribute and parameter_does_not_significantly_impact_attribute: for the two modelled outputs, one assertion per factor on its row of the coefficient table of the selected model; for acidic variants and fragments, which have no adequate model, and for A-Mab concentration, the sentences of the report that state the effect.

The ModularContribution records the platform claim of the step against the cumulative XMuLV requirement; cumulative_value is the sum of the three platform claims the report states, not a measured clearance. The capability of cumulative XMuLV clearance is a property of the train.

The widening of the aggregate criterion of the production bioreactor output by the verification bound of this step is carried by the rows of the worst-case verification table and the report statements of Section 7.7; the bioreactor criterion itself belongs to the annexes of PCR-003 and PCMP-001.
The equipment id equip:vi_sdm_vessel follows the PCP-006 Version 2.0 annex (the Version 1.0 report used equip:vi_sdm).

process_steps.description: Step 6 of the A-Mab drug substance process. The Protein A eluate is adjusted to the inactivation pH, held for the hold time at the set temperature, then neutralized with base and filtered. The hold inactivates enveloped viruses and contributes one of the three claims that meet the cumulative XMuLV requirement, 6.60 log10. The same conditions can add aggregate, fragments and acidic variants, which are formed upstream. No MVM clearance and no host cell protein clearance is claimed for the step. The neutralized pool is the load of cation exchange.

source_references.quote: Low-pH viral inactivation is Step 6 of the A-Mab drug substance process.
The Protein A eluate is held at acid pH for a set time and then neutralized.
The hold inactivates enveloped viruses.
It is adjusted to the inactivation pH, held for the hold time at the set temperature and then neutralized with base.
The neutralized pool is the load of cation exchange.
Development site | Cambridge, MA
Commercial drug substance site | Grafton, WI
Low-pH inactivation claims 6.60 log 10 , anion exchange 5.50 log 10 and virus filtration 4.62 log 10 , which sum to 16.72 log 10 against a requirement of 16.7 log 10 .

The drug substance requires a cumulative clearance of xenotropic murine leukemia virus (XMuLV) of at least 16.7 log 10 , which three steps claim together, and the claim of this step is 6.60 log 10 of it.
The surplus is 0.02 log 10 , so a shortfall at this step larger than that cannot be made up by the other two claims.

parameters.rationale_for_criticality: Classified CPP under SOP-4001 by the decision logic of PCMP-001 §7.7. A rise in pH across the range studied lowers the XMuLV log reduction by 1.22 log10 (p < 0.001), 19 % of the claim, and the claim is lost at the upper edge of the PAR of pH 3.2–3.61. The pH of a large acidified pool is set by acid addition and mixing, the least directly controlled of the three settings, and pH control at manufacturing scale holds about 0.10 pH units, the half-width of the NOR. The margin from the upper NOR edge to the PAR edge is 0.11 pH units, so a drift of the size the NOR allows would reach the PAR edge. No plan sets the margin at which that risk becomes high; on that comparison, a judgement of the report, the risk is high.

design_spaces.definition: The region of inactivation pH, hold time and temperature over which every attribute with a criterion at the step meets it (PCP-006 §7.6), evaluated on a grid of 11 levels of each factor over the ranges studied, 1,331 points in all. Aggregate is inside when both ends of the 95 % prediction interval of a single run lie within its criterion at manufacturing scale, and the XMuLV log reduction is inside when its mean prediction reaches the claim. 63.9 % of the region studied meets the criteria of the two outputs with an adequate model: XMuLV clearance alone rejects 36.1 % of the grid and aggregate none, so the region is bounded by the clearance claim and not by product quality. Acidic variants and fragments have no adequate model and draw no boundary; their measured results meet their criteria across the designs. Judging both modelled outputs on their mean predictions gives the same region. The NOR in force lies inside it, and the region studied is the knowledge space.
